title: Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Berakhot 63b: What was the blessing with which Oved Edom was blessed? That they bore six at one birth. And in Bava Batra 120a: he said, This teaches that she developed the signs of maturity; this teaches that he performed an act of marriage with her. So too it should read in Sotah 12a. And in Sotah, chapter 4, halakhah 4: Rabbi Yuda bar Zevida said, "Yehosef" is written in full. And in Berakhot 12b: Rabbi Abbahu bar Zutrati said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida: They sought to fix the portion of Balak in the Shema, and why did they not fix it? Because of the burden on the public.

And in the Yerushalmi there, chapter 1, halakhah 5, Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said this statement in his name, and there he is called Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevoda. From this Hyman infers that he was a native of the Land of Israel, and everywhere it should read "Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida."

We find that he had two brothers. Rabbi Abba, as in Yevamot 83b: Rabbi Abba, brother of Rabbi Yehuda bar Zavdi, said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda, who said in the name of Rav. And in Kiddushin 43b it reads: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Abba, who said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Zavdi in the name of Rav; it should read as in Yevamot. And Rabbi Simon is his brother, as in the Yerushalmi, Bava Batra, beginning of chapter 3.

notes.text: The body explicitly says he was from the Land of Israel (בר א״י), and Hyman consequently proposes Rabbi rather than the heading’s Rav throughout. His chronology, sibling relationships and proposed transmission-chain correction remain his conclusions.

The inspected Berakhot 63b names Rav Yehudah bar Zevida and specifies a mother-in-law and eight daughters-in-law each bearing six at one birth. Hyman’s shorter plural wording is preserved without adding one wife. His Land-of-Israel, Rabbi-title, sibling and transmission-chain conclusions remain his; the proposed cross-locus identifications are not newly admitted.
